issues.description: Method name mismatch for the Farm song method: the problem statement (UML and task text) names the method printFarmSong(), but the template implementation and reference solution both declare and use singFarmSong(). Specifically, the UML entry in problem_statement.md lists + printFarmSong():void, and the Part 3 task text asks to "Implement the method printFarmSong() inside Farm.java". The template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares public void singFarmSong() (signature at template lines 9-9) and the solution file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java also implements public void singFarmSong() (signature at solution lines 59-59). This naming inconsistency can confuse students about which method to implement and may cause mismatch with automated tests or graders that expect the name used in the problem statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across specification and code. Preferred fixes: (a) Update the problem statement (UML and task text) to refer to singFarmSong() everywhere (recommended, since template and solution already use that name), or (b) rename the method in both template and solution from singFarmSong() to printFarmSong() and update any internal calls. Ensure the UML, task descriptions, template stubs, and reference solution all use the same identifier so students and automated tests expect the same method name.
